newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo banker says U.S. must unblock Yugo funds-Beta.
newsitem.headline: Yugo banker says U.S. must unblock Yugo funds-Beta.

text.p: Yugoslavia must exert pressure on the United States to unblock Yugoslav funds frozen in U.S. banks, independent news agency Beta quoted a top Yugoslav banker as saying Thursday.

"American banks that are holding Yugoslav money although sanctions were lifted a long time ago should even be sued," Beogradska banka director Borka Vucic was quoted as telling a meeting of the Yugoslav Chamber of Commerce Board of Directors.
Vucic said the U.S. blockade of Yugoslav accounts is the basic obstacle to obtaining fresh capital.
She denied reports there is no foreign capital in Yugoslavia but said it is still insufficient.
"There is, however, our capital abroad which we must return," Vucic said and added the state must also do more on recovering outstanding Yugoslav claims abroad.
According to Vucic, foreign credits were granted even during sanctions, but they did not go through banking channels and have already all been repaid. She did not elaborate.

War-related international sanctions against Yugoslavia, comprising Serbia and Montenegro, were lifted in October 1996, but an "outer wall" of sanctions remains in place, barring the country access to world financial and trade organisations.
Vucic said a domestic source of funds lies with the population, but to restore people's confidence in banks the problem of old hard currency savings, frozen since 1991, must first be resolved.
The issue of savings could be resolved with the help of banks that Yugoslavia has founded abroad, Vucic said. -- Amra Kevic, Belgrade newsroom +381 11 222 4305
